idea_text:
Current state-space vision models serialize an image or volume into one or more sequences. Their predictions can consequently depend on an arbitrary traversal: scan direction, rotation, and tile boundaries determine which evidence is compressed first and what survives. The obvious remedy is to add scan directions, raise the state-retention factor toward one, or average schedule-consistent outputs. That only weakens the symptom and either retains serialization or makes convergence arbitrarily slow. Instead, spatial context should be the unique solution of simultaneous local equations, with a separate construction that prevents contraction from attenuating the *value* of evidence merely because it traveled far.

Each pixel or voxel, together with pooled copies at coarser resolutions, is a node in a fixed multiscale graph. Fine nodes connect along principal grid directions and selected dilated offsets; adjacent scales connect through fixed pooling and interpolation incidences. A local encoder produces immutable evidence \(e_i\). All routing decisions depend only on this evidence, never on the iterated context state.

For each directed relation \(r\), the encoder produces scores whose joint incoming normalization is

\[
\alpha_{ijr}(e)=
\frac{\exp a_{ijr}(e)}
{\sum_{(k,s)\in\mathcal N(i)}\exp a_{iks}(e)},
\qquad
\sum_{(j,r)\in\mathcal N(i)}\alpha_{ijr}=1.
\]

Routing can therefore favor a vessel, surface, object boundary, or cross-scale correspondence while retaining a fixed total incoming gain. Relation functions are tied across rotations and reflections when grid equivariance is required.

The ordinary contextual state obeys

\[
h_i=b_\theta(e_i)+q_h\,\sigma\!\left(
\sum_{(j,r)\in\mathcal N(i)}
\alpha_{ijr}(e)U_rh_j
\right),
\qquad 0<q_h<1,
\]

where \(\sigma\) is coordinatewise 1-Lipschitz and

\[
U_r=R_r\operatorname{diag}(\tanh s_r)Q_r^\top
\]

with orthogonal \(R_r,Q_r\). Hence \(\|U_r\|_2\le1\) structurally.

On its own, this branch does impose geometric attenuation on every recurrent path. The refinement is not to relax \(q_h\), but to transport selected evidence together with its own attenuation mass. The encoder emits bounded cargo vectors \(x_i\), nonnegative source strengths \(w_i\), and, if needed, several independently routed cargo groups. For each group, two additional states satisfy

\[
n_i=w_i x_i+
q_t\sum_{(j,r)\in\mathcal N(i)}
\alpha_{ijr}(e)n_j,
\]

\[
d_i=w_i+
q_t\sum_{(j,r)\in\mathcal N(i)}
\alpha_{ijr}(e)d_j,
\qquad 0<q_t<1.
\]

The numerator carries evidence; the denominator carries exactly the same routing mass. Both recurrences remain strict contractions. The decoder reads their quotient

\[
c_i=
\begin{cases}
n_i/d_i,&d_i>0,\\
0,&d_i=0.
\end{cases}
\]

This changes what contraction means. Consider evidence \(x_s\) injected at a source \(s\) and reaching \(i\) through a routed path of length \(k\) and path weight \(p\). Its contributions are

\[
n_i^{(s)}=q_t^k p\,w_sx_s,
\qquad
d_i^{(s)}=q_t^k p\,w_s.
\]

If it is the only evidence reaching that cargo group, then \(c_i=x_s\) exactly, regardless of \(k\), \(q_t\), or \(p\). Contraction suppresses the absolute recurrent state and guarantees convergence, but does not suppress the represented evidence value because attenuation is measured and divided out. With several sources,

\[
c_i=
\frac{\sum_s \rho_{is}x_s}{\sum_s\rho_{is}},
\qquad
\rho_{is}\ge0,
\]

so the output is a well-defined convex average of evidence reaching the node, rather than an exponentially shrinking signal. Distance can still affect competition between sources through \(\rho_{is}\); it no longer forces every remotely transported feature toward zero. Separate cargo groups can represent different anatomical hypotheses, directions, or scales so unrelated sources need not be averaged into one channel.

This is discontinuous from the obvious approach of choosing \(q\) close to one. It retains any fixed contraction margin while converting decay from unwanted feature-amplitude loss into an explicit confidence or support mass \(d_i\). The model can expose \(d_i\) to the decoder, allowing it to distinguish “a stable feature transported with weak support” from “strongly supported context.” Multiscale edges further reduce graph distance, but they are not the primary solution: quotient transport removes path-length attenuation even before that reduction.

The complete state is \(H=(h,n,d)\), equipped with a weighted block-maximum norm, with weights chosen only to reconcile the bounded linear injection between cargo groups if multiple groups interact. In the basic independent construction,

\[
\|H\|=\max\left\{
\max_i\|h_i\|_2,\,
\max_i\|n_i\|_2,\,
\max_i|d_i|
\right\}.
\]

Incoming normalization, \(\|U_r\|_2\le1\), and identity transport in the cargo recurrences give

\[
\|F(H;e)-F(G;e)\|
\le
\max(q_h,q_t)\,\|H-G\|.
\]

Thus a unique equilibrium exists for every input, independently of resolution, graph degree, routing anisotropy, and number of scales. Parallel iteration, raster or reverse sweeps, coarse-to-fine updates, and fair tiled asynchronous updates with bounded communication delay converge to that same equilibrium. Tiled inference must exchange halo states until a global residual criterion is met; one-pass tiling is not claimed to be equivalent.

The quotient does not undermine this convergence result because it is only a readout of the uniquely converged states, not part of their recurrence. At nodes with \(d_i=0\), nonnegativity implies that no positive-strength source has a routed path to the node; then \(n_i=0\) as well, and the cargo output is explicitly defined as absent rather than manufactured. For numerical and certification purposes, division is performed only when a certified lower bound on \(d_i^\star\) is positive. Otherwise that cargo group is withheld and the local and ordinary contextual branches remain available.

Segmentation logits are

\[
z_i=D_\theta(e_i)+V_hh_i^\star+
V_c c_i^\star+\psi_\theta(d_i^\star).
\]

The unrestricted direct term prevents contextual failure from erasing local evidence. Setting both context contributions to zero recovers an ordinary local segmenter. The ordinary equilibrium branch supplies nonlinear global corrections, while quotient transport supplies long-range evidence whose semantic amplitude is not tied to recurrent path length.

The most likely degeneracy is vanishing source mass: the encoder could set every \(w_i=0\), making the transport branch identically absent. This does not corrupt predictions because the direct and ordinary contextual branches remain intact, but it would defeat the intended long-range mechanism. The construction therefore includes non-learned source channels for evidence known to exist everywhere—for example \(w_i=1\) carrying bounded local descriptors—and learned sparse source channels for class- or anatomy-specific evidence. The always-present channels ensure that quotient transport cannot collapse globally; learned channels may legitimately be absent when their proposed evidence is absent.

Approximation remains certifiable. If the joint state estimate \(\widehat H\) has residual \(\varepsilon\), then

\[
\|\widehat H-H^\star\|
\le
\frac{\varepsilon}{1-\max(q_h,q_t)}.
\]

For quotient channel \(i\), interval bounds derived from this state error certify \(d_i^\star\ge\underline d_i>0\). If \(\|x_i\|\le M\), then the equilibrium construction implies \(\|n_i^\star\|\le M d_i^\star\), and standard quotient perturbation bounds give a finite cargo-readout error proportional to \(\varepsilon/\underline d_i\). Nodes lacking a positive denominator certificate receive further updates or omit that cargo contribution. The resulting logit bound can again certify a label whenever its top-two margin exceeds twice the worst-case logit error.

Evaluation should jointly measure segmentation quality, disagreement across solver schedules and tile partitions, convergence residuals, and performance as anatomical separation grows. A decisive test should compare raw transported numerator magnitude against the normalized cargo value: the numerator should decay with route length as required by contraction, while the recovered evidence value should remain stable along correctly routed structures. Rotation equivariance should be evaluated separately from solver invariance.

The central contribution is therefore an order-independent, anisotropic multiscale equilibrium model in which strict contraction still guarantees a unique solution, but selected long-range evidence is carried as a value-plus-mass pair. Geometric damping controls numerical influence and convergence; it no longer automatically erases the content being transported.

idea_text:
Current segmentation systems treat the displayed voxel grid as reality. As a result, the same acquisition reconstructed at different spacings, orientations, or origins can yield different lesion volumes, disconnected components, or disappearance of thin structures. The obvious competent response is resampling augmentation plus a consistency loss. That only encourages approximate agreement on sampled transformations and still allows every rasterization to make an independent, systematically drifting volume prediction.

I propose changing the predicted object. The model predicts an additive class measure on physical acquisition cells, not labels on an output grid. It receives the original acquisition array together with the image-to-world affine, voxel footprints, orientation, and available point-spread metadata. For each physically supported cell \(i\), with physical volume \(V_i\), it outputs a class simplex \(p_{ik}\). The class mass is

\[
m_{ik}=V_i p_{ik},\qquad p_{ik}\geq 0,\qquad \sum_k p_{ik}=1.
\]

An adaptive spatial tree may refine a cell, but a child receives a conditional fraction of its parent’s mass:

\[
m_{ick}=m_{ik}r_{ick},\qquad r_{ick}\geq0,\qquad \sum_c r_{ick}=1.
\]

Thus refinement can localize existing mass but cannot create or destroy it.

### One concrete training iteration

Consider a training example containing:

- an image tensor \(X\) on its native acquisition grid;
- an affine \(A_X\) mapping image-index coordinates into physical coordinates;
- voxel dimensions or full voxel corner geometry;
- scanner metadata, when available;
- one or more ordinary raster masks \(Y^{(a)}\), each with its own affine \(A_Y^{(a)}\), shape, and spacing.

The mask need not have the same resolution, orientation, origin, or extent as the image.

**1. Construct physical image cells.**  
Each native image voxel is interpreted as a physical parallelepiped. Its eight corners are obtained by applying \(A_X\) to the voxel’s index-space corners. If the acquisition has slice gaps, nonuniform slice positions, or another known footprint, those footprints replace the simple parallelepiped construction. The initial prediction cells are these acquisition cells or a predetermined subdivision no finer than the acquisition’s declared support.

The image tensor and physical metadata are passed through the network. For a batch with a fixed native shape, the output is a tensor of logits of shape \([B,K,D,H,W]\). A softmax over \(K\) produces \(p_{ik}\), and multiplication by a precomputed cell-volume tensor produces \(m_{ik}\). Variable geometries can be padded with a validity mask; padded cells participate in neither normalization nor loss.

**2. Interpret the raster annotation physically.**  
Each annotation voxel is also treated as a physical volume, not as a label at a point. For a hard mask, annotation voxel \(j\) defines a piecewise-constant class indicator \(y_{jk}\in\{0,1\}\) over its physical footprint \(R_j\). A probabilistic mask can instead supply \(y_{jk}\in[0,1]\).

No nearest-neighbor resizing is performed. Instead, the data loader computes the physical intersection volume

\[
W_{ij}^{(a)}=\operatorname{Vol}\!\left(C_i\cap R_j^{(a)}\right)
\]

between model cell \(C_i\) and annotation voxel \(R_j^{(a)}\). For affine grids, this is obtained by clipping the corresponding convex polyhedra and measuring the clipped volume. For axis-aligned grids it reduces to products of one-dimensional interval overlaps. Because only nearby cells intersect, the result is stored as a sparse matrix.

This geometry depends only on the two affines and grid shapes, so it can be cached. Its rows also reveal annotation coverage:

\[
c_i^{(a)}=\sum_j W_{ij}^{(a)}.
\]

Cells with \(c_i^{(a)}=0\) are unlabelled rather than background.

**3. Convert the annotation into target class masses.**  
For annotation \(a\), the class mass assigned to prediction cell \(i\) is

\[
t_{ik}^{(a)}=\sum_j W_{ij}^{(a)}y_{jk}^{(a)}.
\]

If the annotation fully covers \(C_i\), then \(\sum_k t_{ik}^{(a)}=V_i\). The target occupancy is

\[
z_{ik}^{(a)}=\frac{t_{ik}^{(a)}}{V_i}.
\]

For partial annotation coverage, the supervised occupancy is instead \(t_{ik}^{(a)}/c_i^{(a)}\), and its loss is weighted by \(c_i^{(a)}/V_i\). This prevents an unannotated portion of a cell from being silently interpreted as background.

This overlap operation is conservative by construction. If one annotation voxel overlaps several model cells, its physical mass is divided among them, and the divided masses sum to the original annotated volume.

**4. Compute the ordinary supervised loss.**  
With a single trusted annotation, the fractional occupancy vector \(z_i\) is a valid categorical distribution. The primary loss is volume-weighted cross-entropy,

\[
L_{\text{exact}}
  =-\sum_i V_i\sum_k z_{ik}\log p_{ik}.
\]

Equivalently, it is cross-entropy between target and predicted class masses after division by cell volume. Fractional targets are not rounded. This is a strictly proper loss for the conditional class occupancy represented by the annotation process: a spatially uniform allocation cannot minimize it unless the conditional target occupancy is actually uniform.

**5. Handle annotation disagreement as interval censoring.**  
If several independent masks are available, each is first mapped through the same physical-overlap calculation, producing occupancies \(z_{ik}^{(1)},\ldots,z_{ik}^{(A)}\). Their disagreement interval is

\[
\ell_{ik}=\min_a z_{ik}^{(a)},\qquad
u_{ik}=\max_a z_{ik}^{(a)}.
\]

The interval is used only for cells genuinely affected by annotator disagreement. Agreement cells retain the exact fractional target. To train on an interval without arbitrarily selecting a boundary, the network additionally predicts a distribution over the uncertain occupancy. For each foreground class it outputs positive Beta parameters \(\alpha_{ik},\beta_{ik}\); its point occupancy remains the mean

\[
p_{ik}=\frac{\alpha_{ik}}{\alpha_{ik}+\beta_{ik}},
\]

with a simplex-valued distribution, such as a Dirichlet, used when mutually exclusive classes must be modeled jointly.

For a Beta marginal, the interval-censored negative log-likelihood is

\[
L_{\text{interval}}
 =-\sum_{i,k} V_i
 \log\!\left[
 F_{\alpha_{ik},\beta_{ik}}(u_{ik})
 -
 F_{\alpha_{ik},\beta_{ik}}(\ell_{ik})
 \right],
\]

where \(F\) is the Beta cumulative distribution function. Numerically, the difference is evaluated in log space. This says that the latent occupancy is observed only to lie in the annotation-supported interval. It does not force the prediction to its midpoint or reward choosing one annotator.

When the individual masks are retained, the stronger implementation trains the predicted occupancy distribution on all individual \(z_{ik}^{(a)}\) values by their log densities; the interval likelihood is reserved for datasets that expose only an uncertainty envelope. This avoids discarding information. Interval likelihood is interpreted under an explicit non-informative censoring assumption; it is not claimed to recover a unique occupancy from a very broad interval.

The total loss combines exact cells, interval-censored cells, and any individually observed occupancies without applying multiple losses to the same evidence. Gradients pass through the softmax or distribution parameters and the network. The sparse geometric-overlap matrix and interval endpoints are fixed target-construction operations and require no gradient.

**6. Supervise refinement only when justified.**  
A parent cell is split only where the annotation or an independent higher-resolution measurement distinguishes its children. Child targets are obtained by intersecting each child footprint with the annotation voxels using the same sparse overlap operation. If the available annotation provides no additional within-parent information, no child localization loss is applied; the model exports the parent mass as spatially unresolved. This prevents raster boundaries from being mistaken for supported subvoxel anatomy.

### Export and invariant

Every requested output grid is derived from the same predicted measure. For output voxel \(Q_q\),

\[
\widehat m_{qk}
 =\sum_i
 \frac{\operatorname{Vol}(Q_q\cap C_i)}{V_i}\,m_{ik},
\]

with the analogous recursive calculation for refined cells. These are conservative geometric intersections, not interpolation of logits or labels. For any output grid that partitions the same physical domain,

\[
\sum_q \widehat m_{qk}=\sum_i m_{ik}.
\]

Consequently, class volumes are identical under reorientation, tiling, pyramid construction, and regridding. Cropping changes the reported volume only by the measure physically outside the crop. A hard mask may be produced at the end using a declared occupancy threshold, but clinical volume measurements use fractional masses directly.

Thin structures can therefore remain as partial mass even when an export grid cannot display them as full voxels. The method does not claim unsupported within-cell geometry; it preserves the amount of tissue while explicitly representing unresolved localization.

The most likely training degeneracy is a spatially uniform allocation, which would satisfy conservation perfectly. It is excluded as a general solution by the cell-level proper loss: conservation constrains how predictions transform, while spatial supervision determines where mass belongs. A separate uncertainty degeneracy can occur if every disagreement interval spans nearly \([0,1]\); such cells contain almost no localization information and are therefore downweighted or left unresolved rather than being allowed to dominate training.

Evaluation repeatedly reconstructs the same acquisitions at different spacings, orientations, origins, and tilings. It measures exact conservation error, variation in clinical volumes, preservation of subvoxel mass, calibration under annotator disagreement, and accuracy against independent high-resolution or pathology references. The contribution is thus discontinuous from augmentation-based robustness: segmentation becomes a physically indexed additive quantity whose volume cannot change merely because the same evidence was rasterized differently.

idea_text:
The obvious competent response to segmentation ambiguity is to estimate voxel probabilities, ensemble variance, or several sampled masks and then report empirical variation. That approach cannot establish that an unseen, globally coherent alternative mask would not reverse a clinical conclusion. The proposed system instead releases only conclusions shared by every complete segmentation admitted by a calibrated, exactly searchable hypothesis class. Its discontinuous causal lever is universal quantification over whole masks, not better local uncertainty estimation.

To make that quantification exact rather than computationally aspirational, the method deliberately does not permit arbitrary labeling of a full 3D voxel grid. Exact connectivity and component-count optimization over unrestricted 3D labelings is NP-hard, so no choice of generic integer solver removes the worst-case problem. Instead, each scan is deterministically converted into a 3D cell complex whose cells are unions of voxels and whose adjacency graph is constrained during construction to have treewidth at most a fixed constant \(w\). Cells may be small near image edges and clinically important structures and large in homogeneous interiors, but the treewidth cap is inviolable. The reported segmentation is a union of these cells; consequently, all guarantees apply to this explicitly stated annotation resolution rather than to arbitrary subcell boundaries. Reference masks are converted by a fixed, preregistered cell-labeling rule before calibration and evaluation, so calibration and deployment concern the same structured target.

For cell \(v\), let \(z_v\in\{1,\ldots,L\}\) be its label. The complete-mask energy is

\[
E_x(z)=
\sum_{v} a_v^x(z_v)
+\sum_{(u,v)\in A} b_{uv}^x(z_u,z_v)
+\sum_{h\in H} c_h^x(z_h),
\]

where \(A\) is cell adjacency and each higher-order factor \(h\) lies wholly inside a bag of a supplied width-\(w\) tree decomposition. Unary terms encode image evidence. Pairwise terms encode boundary evidence and allowed label interfaces. Bounded-arity bag factors encode local anatomical rules, such as which tissues may meet or which side of a known compartment interface a label may occupy. Forbidden configurations receive infinite cost. The construction excludes unrestricted dense interactions and unrestricted global shape penalties, because either would invalidate the tractability claim.

All finite factor costs are nonnegative integers in \(\{0,\ldots,K\}\), with fixed \(K\). A network may predict real scores, but a fixed quantizer maps them to these integers before both calibration and deployment. Thus the total finite energy is at most \(M=O(nK)\), up to a constant determined by the bounded number of factors per cell. This bounded integer range is essential: even an energy-constrained optimization on a path can encode knapsack if arbitrary-precision costs are allowed.

Exact inference uses dynamic programming on a nice tree decomposition. A table state records:

- the labels of cells currently exposed in the bag;
- for each relevant foreground label, a partition of exposed cells describing which are already connected through the processed subgraph;
- flags indicating whether a connected component has been completely closed;
- any finite-state anatomical information required by a queried relation, such as whether a lesion component has touched a critical structure;
- accumulated integer energy \(e\in\{0,\ldots,M\}\).

Introduce, forget, and join operations update labels, connectivity partitions, closed-component counts, and energy exactly. When a cell is forgotten, a component is counted precisely when its final representative disappears from the separator. Join nodes merge connectivity partitions while correcting quantities counted in both children. Because a bag contains at most \(w+1\) cells, the number of labelings and partitions per bag depends exponentially only on fixed \(w\), not on volume size. Runtime is polynomial in the number of cells and \(M\), with a factor of roughly \(L^{w+1}\) times the number of bag partitions. The width cap and bounded integer costs therefore make the algorithm fixed-parameter and pseudo-polynomial in a quantity already bounded polynomially by construction; it is not an appeal to favorable mixed-integer solver behavior.

The minimum energy \(E^*(x)\) is obtained from the same dynamic program. On a held-out calibration set, compute

\[
R_i=E_{x_i}(z_i)-E^*(x_i),
\]

where \(z_i\) is the deterministically cell-encoded expert segmentation. A split-conformal quantile \(q\) defines

\[
\mathcal S(x)=\{z:E_x(z)\le E^*(x)+q\}.
\]

Under exchangeability, the complete encoded reference mask lies in this set with the selected marginal probability. The energy need not be probabilistically calibrated.

Each requested certificate is then another exact pass over the same decomposition, retaining only states with final energy at most \(E^*(x)+q\). Additive quantities such as lesion volume are updated by adding each cell’s voxel volume. Component count is updated when components close. Contact with a critical structure is a local adjacency flag. Connectivity between specified anatomical terminals is read from the final connectivity partition. Vessel continuity is made precise as a declared graph predicate—for example, whether labeled vessel cells connect two specified inlet and outlet regions—not as an informal visual notion. The dynamic program minimizes and maximizes each quantity over all feasible states. For a voxel or cell label, it tests whether any feasible mask assigns each competing class. A label is released only if exactly one class is feasible.

This supports statements such as: every plausible lesion mask has volume above a treatment threshold; every plausible vessel segmentation connects the declared endpoints; no plausible tumor component contacts the protected structure; or the lesion has between two and four components. The dynamic-programming tables and backpointers constitute checkable certificates that the extrema range over every representable mask below the calibrated energy threshold, rather than over samples found by a decoder.

If the encoded true mask belongs to \(\mathcal S(x)\), every universally agreed cell label is simultaneously correct, and every optimized interval contains that mask’s corresponding quantity. One conformal event therefore jointly protects any number of conclusions derived by universal quantification; no multiplicity correction across those conclusions is required.

The main likely degeneration is not a hidden all-zero optimization state but an overly large threshold \(q\), caused by a poorly ranked energy or a coarse representation. Then nearly all grammar-compatible masks are feasible, intervals widen, and decisions are withheld. The algorithm cannot turn that failure into false confidence because it still enumerates the complete feasible state space. Experiments should separately report encoded whole-mask coverage, cell resolution and representation error relative to native annotations, treewidth and runtime, certifiable tissue fraction, clinical interval width, component/connectivity decision-release rates, and abstention under scanner or pathology shift. Exchangeability failure remains an explicit deployment limitation; exact optimization does not repair distribution shift.

idea_text:
Longitudinal medical segmentation should be formulated as estimating tissue change, not repeatedly drawing unrelated masks. Independent segmentations of serial scans can convert registration error, slice-thickness changes, and boundary noise into spurious lesion growth or disappearance, even when each mask has good cross-sectional overlap.

The proposed method represents each tissue class by a continuous occupancy density in physical coordinates and jointly estimates a deformation field between visits and a local source term describing genuine creation or loss of that tissue. These quantities must satisfy a discretized continuity equation: occupancy at the later visit equals transported earlier occupancy plus the integrated source term. The numerical discretization uses finite-volume fluxes, so the identity is exact: total predicted volume change equals net boundary flux plus the summed source term, independent of voxel spacing or internal resampling. Segmentations at individual visits are readouts of these jointly constrained densities rather than separately generated masks.

The crucial intervention is to make deformation and biological change observationally distinguishable during acquisition or training. The source term is permitted only where registered image evidence changes in a way that cannot be explained by the estimated deformation and the scanner’s known point-spread and intensity-transfer model. Regions lacking such evidence are transported but cannot spontaneously gain or lose tissue. Conversely, the deformation is constrained to be invertible and spatially regular, so it cannot explain a genuinely appearing lesion by folding or deleting anatomy. Cases that remain non-identifiable—such as a new lesion below both scans’ resolution—are explicitly reported as unresolved rather than assigned zero change. Manual longitudinal annotations can supervise occupancy and source terms where available, but the conservation identity itself does not depend on learned calibration.

The most obvious approach is to register scans and then add a temporal-consistency loss between ordinary segmentations. That encourages similarity but provides no account of where measured volume change came from and can suppress real progression. Here, transport and biological change are separate variables linked by a conservation law, making every predicted change attributable: motion crosses region boundaries, while creation or destruction appears as a source term.

The likely degeneracy is assigning all differences to either deformation or source. It is blocked structurally rather than by an arbitrary trade-off alone: invertibility and bounded strain limit deformation, the image-formation residual limits where sources are admissible, and unresolved cases are allowed to remain set-valued. Evaluation would therefore test not only Dice, but conservation residuals, recovery of known synthetic growth under realistic acquisition changes, false progression on scan–rescan pairs, and accuracy of clinically relevant longitudinal volume-change estimates.

final_idea_core.mechanism: Jointly estimate a continuous occupancy density, an inter-visit deformation field, and a local tissue creation/loss source term, all linked by a discretized continuity equation.

idea_text:
Clinical segmentation often reports a precise boundary where CT physics does not identify one. For a small pulmonary nodule or a thin enhancing margin, multiple subvoxel occupancies can produce indistinguishable measurements after projection, partial-volume mixing, detector blur, scatter, and noise. A better network can select a plausible boundary but cannot establish that the measurements require it.

The proposed method reports **measurement-consistent inner and outer segmentations**. Its central move is not predictive uncertainty or sampling masks: it computes what is logically forced or permitted by the acquired projection data.

For a prespecified region around the lesion, partition physical space into cells and let \(o_j\in[0,1]\) denote target-material occupancy in cell \(j\). Introduce attenuation variables \(x_j\), rather than optimizing unknown attenuation coefficients jointly with occupancy. Calibration supplies target and background attenuation intervals \([\mu_T^-,\mu_T^+]\) and \([\mu_B^-,\mu_B^+]\). Occupancy and attenuation are connected by the linear inequalities

\[
\mu_B^-+( \mu_T^- -\mu_B^- )o_j
\le x_j \le
\mu_B^+ +( \mu_T^+ -\mu_B^+ )o_j .
\]

Thus all permitted target/background mixtures are represented without bilinear products between occupancy and unknown material coefficients. Multi-material cases use nonnegative material-fraction variables summing to one, with corresponding linear attenuation bounds.

The raw photon counts are first converted into certified intervals on nominal line integrals. Poisson count intervals, bounded incident intensity, scatter, dark current, and gain uncertainty are propagated through the monotone negative-log transformation using outward-rounded interval arithmetic. Effects that do not remain linear after this transformation—including uncertain focal-spot blur, detector response, and geometry—are not optimized as explicit nuisance variables. Instead, calibration establishes a certified per-ray discrepancy bound \(d_i\) between the true scanner response and a fixed nominal projection matrix \(A\), uniformly over the allowed attenuation range. These bounds can be computed offline by interval propagation through the full scanner simulator or by worst-case calibration measurements. If the resulting transformed-data interval is \([\ell_i,u_i]\), the admissible set is the polytope

\[
\mathcal P =
\left\{
(o,x):
0\le o\le1,\quad
\ell_i-d_i\le (Ax)_i\le u_i+d_i\ \forall i,\quad
L_j(o_j)\le x_j\le U_j(o_j)
\right\}.
\]

Optional assumptions such as a known maximum lesion extent or bounded total variation may be included only when they are independently prespecified and expressible as linear constraints. Learned plausibility scores are excluded. A network may propose a computational region, but guarantee-bearing computation must also include a conservative enclosing region and fixed bounds for attenuation outside it; otherwise cropping could invalidate coverage.

This polytope is a conservative outer approximation of the full nonlinear physical feasible set. It is not claimed to reproduce that set exactly. The crucial invariant is inclusion: calibration is designed so that every allowed scanner configuration and noise realization maps the true occupancy and attenuation into \(\mathcal P\). Enlarging the physical set can widen reported intervals, but cannot create false certainty.

For each cell, the reported bounds are the exact linear-program extrema

\[
\underline o_j=\min_{(o,x)\in\mathcal P}o_j,
\qquad
\overline o_j=\max_{(o,x)\in\mathcal P}o_j.
\]

The inner segmentation contains cells with \(\underline o_j\ge\tau\); the outer segmentation contains cells with \(\overline o_j\ge\tau\). Total target volume is bounded directly by minimizing and maximizing \(\sum_j v_j o_j\), rather than summing independently optimized cell bounds. Contact with an anatomical surface is reported only when a corresponding constrained feasibility problem proves contact unavoidable or impossible.

These programs do not require two independent full reconstructions per cell. They share one sparse constraint matrix and differ only in their objective vectors. A primal-dual interior-point solve first finds a feasible central point and reusable matrix factorization or preconditioner. Coordinate objectives are then processed in batches with warm starts. More importantly, dual feasible solutions provide certified lower and upper bounds before convergence: cells are stopped as soon as their dual certificates place them definitively above or below the clinical threshold. Only ambiguous boundary cells require tight optimization. Adaptive spatial refinement splits those cells while preserving parent-cell mass constraints. Final claims use primal and dual residuals checked with directed rounding; if a solver cannot certify a bound, that cell remains unresolved rather than inheriting a heuristic result. Clinical quantities usually require only two additional LPs each.

The most likely degeneracy is not solver failure but an overly conservative scanner-discrepancy envelope: loose \(d_i\) values can make the inner region empty and the outer region large. This does not collapse to an incorrect mask. It explicitly reports that the acquisition does not resolve the boundary. Calibration phantoms, repeated blank scans, and scanner-specific attenuation limits can tighten the envelope, but no learned prior is allowed to override it.

Under the calibration coverage assumptions, the true latent object lies in \(\mathcal P\). Therefore every minimum is no greater than the true occupancy, every maximum is no smaller, and optimized clinical quantities bracket their true values by construction. This is discontinuous from the obvious competent approach—training a higher-resolution segmenter with uncertainty heads—because the output is determined by certified inversion of the measurement process, not by a model’s distribution over plausible anatomy.

Evaluation would first use simulated CT with exact subvoxel geometry and deliberately varied scanner nuisance parameters, then physical anthropomorphic phantoms. The primary metrics are empirical containment coverage, interval width, and the frequency with which threshold decisions receive valid dual certificates. Retrospective raw-data studies would then test whether conventional precise masks lie outside the boundaries actually defensible from the measurements.

idea_text:
High-resolution 3D segmentation should be treated as an output-sensitive computation problem: large homogeneous regions should not require the same work as boundaries, thin structures, and small lesions. Unlike learned cropping or token pruning, however, computation should be omitted only when it is provably irrelevant to the output of a fully specified dense model.

The segmentation model is constructed as an image-conditioned multiresolution logit field rather than as a deep network through which spatial intervals must be propagated. An unrestricted encoder computes a global conditioning vector and coefficient grids at several resolutions. The encoder may be deep because it is run once; certification never propagates spatial intervals through it. For voxel coordinate \(x\), class \(c\) has logit

\[
\ell_c(x)=b_c(g)+\sum_{s=1}^{S} I_s(A_{s,c},x),
\]

where \(g\) is the global image representation, \(A_{s,c}\) is an image-conditioned 3D coefficient grid, and \(I_s\) is trilinear interpolation. Fine grids can be predicted from correspondingly local image-pyramid features, while coarse grids carry global context. The exhaustive reference prediction is simply \(\arg\max_c\ell_c(x)\) at every scanner-native voxel.

Certification operates directly on pairwise logit differences. For candidate class \(c\) against competitor \(j\),

\[
d_{cj}(x)=b_c(g)-b_j(g)+
\sum_s I_s(A_{s,c}-A_{s,j},x).
\]

For an axis-aligned query box \(B\), enumerate the interpolation cells intersecting \(B\). A trilinear function attains its extrema over each clipped cell at the clipped cell’s vertices. Evaluating the difference grid’s trilinear interpolant at those vertices therefore gives valid per-scale bounds \(L^s_{cj}(B)\) and \(U^s_{cj}(B)\). Summing the bounds gives

\[
L_{cj}(B)=b_c(g)-b_j(g)+\sum_s L^s_{cj}(B).
\]

If \(L_{cj}(B)>0\) for every \(j\neq c\), every voxel in \(B\) is provably assigned class \(c\), so the box can be emitted without pointwise evaluation. Otherwise it is subdivided.

These extrema can be obtained without scanning all coefficients in a large box. Each difference grid maintains a range-minimum/range-maximum hierarchy over interpolation-cell extrema. Fully covered nodes are queried from the hierarchy; only cells intersecting the box boundary require explicit clipped-vertex evaluation. The resulting bounds are deterministic properties of the already-computed coefficient grids, not predictions from another routing model.

This construction avoids catastrophic deep-IBP expansion by design. Spatial uncertainty passes through no learned matrix products, nonlinear activations, or repeated dependency-losing interval transformations. Each scale contributes one exact or conservative interpolation range, and the only relaxation is addition across scales. Thus width can grow additively with multiscale residual variation, but not exponentially with network depth. Strictly non-negative classifier weights are unnecessary because certification is performed on the final pairwise difference fields rather than by separately bounding latent channels through a classification head. The deliberate architectural restriction is that all spatially varying computation must end in additive interpolation fields; arbitrary global computation is allowed only through quantities constant over the queried box.

Training uses ordinary voxelwise cross-entropy and Dice or boundary losses on exhaustive evaluations, so the underlying dense predictor is trained normally. Two additional losses improve early termination without defining correctness. First, sample axis-aligned boxes lying entirely inside a single ground-truth region and penalize violations of a certified margin:

\[
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{box}}
=\sum_{B}\sum_{j\neq y_B}
\max\!\left(0,m-L_{y_Bj}(B)\right).
\]

Second, penalize the unresolved width only for such interior boxes,

\[
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{width}}
=\sum_B\sum_{j\neq y_B}
\bigl(U_{y_Bj}(B)-L_{y_Bj}(B)\bigr),
\]

with boxes sampled across physical sizes. Boundary-crossing boxes receive no pressure to become homogeneous. The full objective is the dense segmentation loss plus weighted box-margin and width terms. Because the dense loss remains present and the auxiliary losses apply only where the annotation is homogeneous, reducing interval width cannot substitute for learning lesion boundaries. Ablations should separately test the accuracy–termination trade-off as the auxiliary weights vary.

The component most likely to degenerate is the additive multiscale bound: unrelated extrema from different scales may occur at different coordinates, making their summed interval too loose. This can reduce early termination, but it cannot create a false certificate. Moreover, computation is capped: once an unresolved box reaches a fixed tile size, all voxels in that tile are evaluated in one dense batch rather than continuing voxel-by-voxel recursion. An octree with this stopping rule contains only a constant-factor number of nodes relative to the number of fallback tiles, so even completely uninformative certificates reduce to bounded-overhead exhaustive inference rather than an astronomically expensive search. Native-cell evaluation remains available when exact masks require it.

Small lesions are therefore protected structurally. A box containing voxels with different exhaustive labels cannot satisfy a valid common-class dominance certificate and must be refined or densely evaluated. For approximate clinical outputs, recursion can instead stop when unresolved volume is below a declared tolerance; surface extraction can discard certified interiors and refine only boxes that may contain label transitions.

The most obvious competent response to loose bounds would be to apply stronger IBP, Lipschitz regularization, or non-negative layers to an ordinary deep segmentation network. That still asks intervals to survive a long spatial computation graph. The discontinuous move here is to make the final segmentation itself a range-queryable spatial field: deep learning produces its coefficients, but certification begins only after that field exists. Experiments should measure exact identity with exhaustive inference, termination rate by box size, runtime against boundary complexity, sensitivity to the auxiliary losses, and worst-case overhead when every certificate fails.

final_idea_core.core_claim: Certification operates on a post-hoc, range-queryable logit field, rather than propagating spatial uncertainty through the deep neural network's internal layers, avoiding the catastrophic expansion of interval bounds inherent in deep IBP.
final_idea_core.mechanism: A multiresolution logit field, whose coefficients are predicted by a deep encoder, directly provides provable logit difference bounds over axis-aligned query boxes, enabling early termination in regions where a single class is dominant.
final_idea_core.problem_targeted: High-resolution 3D medical image segmentation requires significant redundant computation in homogeneous regions, yet traditional learned methods struggle to provably omit this work without compromising accuracy or incurring prohibitive verification costs.
final_idea_core.source_gap: The additive combination of per-scale interpolation bounds for logit differences, though potentially loose, remains informative enough to enable significant early termination without introducing false positives.
final_idea_core.expected_effect: The proposed method will achieve exact identity with exhaustive inference while significantly reducing computation time, especially in anatomically simple or homogeneous regions, scaling runtime according to boundary complexity rather than volume.

idea_text:
Medical segmenters often fail after scanner, reconstruction, or acquisition-protocol changes that preserve anatomy but alter numerical intensity calibration. The standard competent response is to retain intensities and approximate robustness through normalization, histogram matching, augmentation, or domain adaptation. Those methods only cover transformations represented during training. The proposed intervention is discontinuous from that approach: remove intensity magnitude before learning, so an entire nuisance class is mathematically incapable of changing the prediction.

For each modality, preprocessing converts the image into a dense multiscale ordinal representation. Every voxel stores its tie-aware global rank and local ranks within several fixed physical-radius neighborhoods. At each scale, comparisons are defined on a fixed sparse stencil containing short-range 3D offsets, larger dilated offsets, and fixed correspondences between adjacent scales. For every within-scale offset \(\delta\), preprocessing creates three dense binary mask volumes:

\[
M_{\delta,-}(p),\quad M_{\delta,0}(p),\quad M_{\delta,+}(p),
\]

indicating whether the neighbor at \(p+\delta\) is respectively darker than, equal to, or brighter than the voxel at \(p\). Exactly one mask is active wherever both locations are valid. Coarse cells are represented by an order statistic such as their median, and cross-scale masks compare these coarse representatives with their fixed child locations. No connection is chosen from intensity magnitude.

The network uses a dense-grid ordinal convolution, not message passing over a materialized graph. Let \(h_s\) be the dense feature tensor at scale \(s\). For every offset \(\delta\), a standard tensor shift produces the complete shifted volume

\[
H_{s,\delta}(p)=h_s(p+\delta).
\]

This is implemented by padding and fixed slicing, or equivalently by a one-hot depthwise 3D convolution; it requires no index arrays, scatter, gather, adjacency matrices, or input-dependent routing. The responses for all three ordinal states are then computed everywhere:

\[
Y_{s,\delta,r}
=
H_{s,\delta}\odot k_{s,\delta,r},
\qquad r\in\{-,0,+\},
\]

where \(k_{s,\delta,r}\) is a learned channel-wise depthwise coefficient. Only afterward are they multiplexed per voxel by the precomputed dense masks:

\[
\widetilde Y_s
=
\sum_{\delta\in\mathcal D_s}
\sum_{r\in\{-,0,+\}}
M_{s,\delta,r}\odot Y_{s,\delta,r}.
\]

Thus darker, equal, and brighter responses are all evaluated globally with dense tensor operations, and a one-hot mask selects the appropriate response at each location. The layer is

\[
z_s
=
A_s h_s
+
P_s\!\left(
\widetilde Y_s+
\sum_{\delta,r}
M_{s,\delta,r}\odot
g_{s,\delta,r}
\right)
+
Q_s(\widetilde Y_s^{\mathrm{cross}}),
\]

followed by channel normalization, a pointwise gated nonlinearity, and a residual connection. Here \(P_s\) is a shared \(1\times1\times1\) channel mixer, while \(g_{s,\delta,r}\) is a learned projection of bounded Fourier features of the fixed relative physical displacement. Coordinates influence responses but never determine ordinal states.

Cross-scale communication is also strictly dense. Fixed strided convolution, geometry-only interpolation, and dense one-hot cross-scale comparison masks align parent and child grids. The three possible parent–child responses are computed over the entire aligned grid and multiplexed exactly as above. Invalid boundary locations are suppressed by fixed validity masks.

The resulting cost is \(O(N|\mathcal D|C)\) before the pointwise channel mixer, with fixed storage per voxel. Implementations may stack the three state responses into an extra tensor axis and perform one fused mask-and-reduction operation. All spatial operations are dense shifts, depthwise convolutions, elementwise products, reductions, interpolation, and \(1\times1\times1\) convolutions. The fixed stencil describes which dense shifts are computed, but no graph data structure exists at runtime.

A U-shaped encoder and decoder built entirely from these layers produces voxelwise logits. Downsampling partitions space into fixed physical cells and applies order statistics to ordinal labels; upsampling uses geometry-only interpolation. Skip connections join matching ordinal feature grids. Dilated offsets and coarse scales propagate information over long distances without attention or adaptive edge selection.

Initial voxel features contain modality embeddings, voxel geometry, normalized physical coordinates, tie-aware ranks, and local ordinal summaries. Exact rank information is retained as integer lower rank, upper rank, and tie count. These integers are represented losslessly by deterministic bit planes before a learned linear projection; local quantile fractions supplement rather than replace them. Raw intensity, intensity differences, moments, histogram bins, and learned magnitude thresholds are never exposed.

The invariance is established by construction. Let each modality undergo an arbitrary strictly increasing transformation \(f\). Such a transformation preserves all pairwise comparisons, ties, order statistics, global ranks, and local ranks. It also leaves geometry and modality identity unchanged. Therefore every rank feature and every dense categorical mask is bitwise identical before and after transformation. Since every later operation receives identical tensors, induction through the network gives identical hidden features and segmentation logits for every possible setting of the learned weights.

For images without ties, the complete global ordering is a maximal invariant: two finite arrays have the same ordering exactly when their observed values can be related by a strictly increasing remapping. Sparse spatial masks therefore do not weaken the invariance claim, because lossless global ranks remain available at every voxel. The masks supply efficient spatial interaction conditioned on ordinal relations, while the ranks preserve the full monotone-invariant intensity information.

The component most likely to degenerate is ordinal preprocessing in nearly homogeneous tissue. Small contrast does not by itself make the representation zero: any consistent nonzero ordering remains encoded exactly in ranks and comparison masks, and coarse and dilated comparisons propagate it spatially. The representation becomes uninformative only when measurements are genuinely tied, in which case equality masks and tie counts correctly state that no intensity-defined boundary is identifiable. It can also become unstable when noise reverses order. That limitation is explicit: the method guarantees invariance to global modality-wise monotone calibration, not to noise, spatially varying bias fields, contrast inversion, or reconstruction changes that alter local ordering. Equality may use scanner-declared quantization equivalence, but not an intensity-distance threshold, because such a threshold would destroy exact monotone invariance.

The central experiment would train on one scanner set and test on held-out institutions and on copies transformed by strictly increasing splines far outside the training distribution. The construction check is bitwise identity of all ordinal tensors and prediction logits under those transformations. Baselines would include normalization, histogram matching, broad monotone augmentation, and domain adaptation. Contrast inversion, spatially varying bias fields, pre-remapping noise, and texture-changing reconstruction are negative controls that should alter the representation. The expected result is unconditional immunity to global monotone calibration changes and improved institutional transfer specifically when such calibration is a dominant source of shift.

final_idea_core.mechanism: The method preprocesses medical images into dense, multiscale ordinal representations, entirely removing intensity magnitude information before neural network learning, ensuring mathematical invariance to monotone intensity transformations.
final_idea_core.problem_targeted: Medical image segmenters fail under shifts in scanner calibration, reconstruction, or acquisition protocols that alter intensity magnitudes but preserve anatomy and ordinal relationships.
final_idea_core.source_gap: The critical information for medical image segmentation is encoded in the relative ordering of voxel intensities and geometric arrangements, not their absolute magnitudes, and these ordinal relationships are robust to relevant noise and acquisition variat…
final_idea_core.expected_effect: The system will exhibit unconditional immunity to global monotone calibration changes and demonstrably improved institutional transfer performance specifically when such calibration shifts are the primary source of domain discrepancy.

idea_text:
False-positive lesion components are especially dangerous in high-resolution CT segmentation: a model can draw a spatially coherent, anatomically plausible lesion from reconstruction artifacts, and ordinary confidence scores are not independent evidence because they are produced from the same image that generated the lesion. The most obvious approach is therefore to improve uncertainty calibration or suppress small components. Instead, the proposed method asks whether each predicted lesion leaves a detectable signature in raw scanner measurements that were never available when that lesion was proposed.

For CT acquisitions with photon-counting data, randomly divide every measured ray count by binomial thinning. If the original count is Poisson, the two resulting counts are independent Poisson observations with proportionally reduced exposures. Reconstruct the first subset and run any segmentation system on it. This produces fixed candidate lesion components, along with their locations and supports, without seeing the second subset.

Each candidate is then tested against the held-out counts using the calibrated CT forward model. Construct two physical explanations before inspecting those counts. The alternative permits an attenuation change within the proposed component, with its attenuation profile and surrounding anatomy estimated only from the proposal subset. The null forbids a lesion-specific change there but permits a prespecified set of nuisance explanations, including smooth background attenuation, beam-hardening parameters, and bounded registration or calibration errors. For held-out measurement vector \(y\), compute a likelihood ratio whose numerator is the fixed alternative predictive density and whose denominator is the pointwise maximum density over the allowed null nuisance set:

\[
e(y)=\frac{p_{\mathrm{alt}}(y)}
{\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{null}}}p_\theta(y)}.
\]

For any true null parameter in the declared nuisance set, this is a valid e-value because the denominator is at least the true null density and therefore \(\mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{null}}[e]\leq 1\). Apply an e-value multiple-testing procedure across all proposed components and retain only components receiving independent measurement support at a chosen false-discovery-rate level. The retained component’s detailed boundary still comes from the segmenter; the test certifies evidence for the component’s existence, not voxel-perfect boundary correctness. Components that cannot be distinguished from the nuisance model are explicitly reported as unresolved rather than silently deleted or accepted.

The step most likely to degenerate is the held-out test becoming powerless after photon splitting. This does not create false validity: it produces unresolved candidates. Power can be measured as a function of lesion contrast, size, and split fraction, and the system should be restricted to acquisition regimes where clinically relevant lesions have adequate held-out detectability. Crucially, repeated adaptive splitting of the same counts would invalidate independence and is not allowed; the random split is fixed before reconstruction and proposal generation.

The central contribution is to turn lesion segmentation into proposal followed by independent physical replication within a single acquisition. Unlike calibrated confidence, ensembles, topology constraints, or component-size filtering, a hallucinated component must explain unseen projection counts under scanner physics before it can be reported as measurement-supported. Evaluation would measure component-level false discovery, sensitivity versus effective dose, and robustness to reconstruction artifacts, while separately reporting boundary accuracy for the surviving components.

final_idea_core.core_claim: It transforms lesion segmentation into a two-stage process of proposal generation followed by independent physical replication, where a proposed lesion must explain unseen raw scanner measurements.
final_idea_core.mechanism: The method splits raw photon-counting CT data into two independent subsets, uses one for segmentation to propose candidate lesions, and then evaluates each candidate against the held-out subset using a physical likelihood ratio test based on a calibrated…
final_idea_core.problem_targeted: High-resolution CT segmentation models can generate false-positive lesion components from reconstruction artifacts, which are difficult to identify because standard confidence scores are not independent evidence.
final_idea_core.source_gap: Clinically relevant lesions must leave a detectable signature in the held-out raw scanner measurements, even after photon splitting, with sufficient power to distinguish them from nuisance explanations.
final_idea_core.expected_effect: The system will reduce component-level false positives in CT lesion segmentation by only retaining components that receive independent measurement support at a chosen false-discovery-rate level, while maintaining sensitivity for true lesions.

idea_text:
The most obvious response to a deterministic-policy plateau is to increase token entropy, perturb parameters, or sample more continuations from the original prompt. All three search within the policy induced by one representation. The proposed causal lever is discontinuous from that approach: search over certified symmetries of the problem itself, because the same low-entropy model can enter different reasoning basins when an exactly equivalent problem is presented differently.

This applies to domains with executable or formal semantics. For each problem \(x\), construct transformations \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\) that preserve solvability, such as symbol renaming, permutation of interchangeable objects, unit rescaling, coordinate changes, reordering independent assumptions, and proof-assistant-checked expression rewrites. Every admitted transformation must provide:

1. a transformed problem \(g_i(x)\);
2. an inverse map from completed solutions on \(g_i(x)\) to solutions on \(x\);
3. for dynamic scheduling, a certified map \(C_i\) from intermediate verifier states on \(g_i(x)\) into a common state space associated with \(x\).

The third requirement is stronger than merely transforming final answers. A transformation is eligible for divergence-based scheduling only when its intermediate states can be transported. For symbolic proofs, \(C_i\) inversely substitutes symbols and coordinates in the current assumptions, goals, and derived facts, then applies the verifier’s normalizer. For programs, it inversely maps variables and values and records canonical executed states. The map must preserve semantic validity: every mapped fact must be derivable from the original assumptions, as checked by the symbolic engine. Transformations lacking such a state map remain usable for uniform complete rollouts but cannot receive divergence-based priority.

During one reinforcement-learning search step for an unsolved problem, compute is scheduled as follows.

First, sample a fixed set of certified transformations, including the identity. Give every representation the same initial budget of \(k\) prefixes, each advanced for \(h\) verifier actions. Generation is constrained to an interface in which each proposed proof action, program statement, or formal derivation step is executed immediately. Invalid actions terminate that prefix. Free-form explanatory text is ignored by the scheduling signal.

Second, after every accepted action, obtain the resulting verifier state \(s_{i,j,t}\), where \(i\) identifies the representation, \(j\) the rollout, and \(t\) the step. Map it on the fly to

\[
z_{i,j,t}=N(C_i(s_{i,j,t})),
\]

where \(N\) is deterministic semantic normalization. A proof-state fingerprint contains normalized open goals and the normalized derived facts relevant to those goals. A program-state fingerprint contains the normalized control location and observable symbolic store. Thus, renaming \(a\) to \(b\) or reordering assumptions produces the same fingerprint, while introducing a new lemma, decomposition, invariant, or subgoal produces a different one.

Third, compare behavior using the canonical state sequences, not generated text. For each prefix, retain the set of fingerprints it visited and its final canonical state. Define its distance from another prefix as a weighted combination of:

\[
1-\frac{|S_p\cap S_q|}{|S_p\cup S_q|}
\]

for visited-state-set difference, and normalized tree-edit distance between their final open-goal structures. All quantities are computed from verifier objects. The weights and normalization are fixed before training; neither is learned from reward.

Fourth, calculate a representation’s scheduling score from two terms. The first is marginal coverage: the number of canonical fingerprints produced by that representation that have not yet appeared in any other representation for the current problem. The second is separation: the mean distance from each of its surviving prefixes to its nearest prefix generated under another representation. Marginal coverage detects genuinely new semantic regions, while nearest-prefix separation prevents a large family of nearly duplicate trajectories from appearing diverse merely because it has more samples. Scores are divided by rollout tokens already spent on that representation, so the scheduler estimates new semantic coverage per unit compute.

Fifth, distribute the next compute tranche explicitly. A fixed fraction \(\epsilon\) is divided uniformly among all representations; the remaining \(1-\epsilon\) is allocated proportionally to their nonnegative coverage-per-compute scores. If every score is zero, the whole tranche is allocated uniformly. Within a representation, half of its tranche extends prefixes whose final canonical states are farthest from the current global state set, and half starts fresh prefixes. This prevents an initially unusual but dead-end prefix from consuming the entire budget. Extension proceeds for another \(h\) accepted actions, states are remapped, scores are recomputed, and allocation repeats until the per-problem budget is exhausted or a solution is found. A minimum uniform allocation and fresh-prefix allocation ensure that the novelty signal changes efficiency but cannot eliminate ordinary search.

Whenever a representation yields a completed solution \(y\), the system computes \(g_i^{-1}(y)\) and runs the original verifier:

\[
V(g_i(x),y)=1
\quad\text{and}\quad
V(x,g_i^{-1}(y))=1.
\]

Only after both checks pass does the trajectory enter training. Successful trajectories are transported to the original coordinates and deduplicated by their canonical state sequence. They may then receive the ordinary terminal correctness reward in an on-policy update or be used as verified solution demonstrations. Behavioral divergence never contributes reward and cannot turn an incorrect trajectory into a positive example; it only schedules search.

The mechanism can escape a low-entropy plateau because equivalent representations can activate computations that are distant in token space. A geometry problem may deterministically elicit an unsuccessful synthetic argument in its original presentation but a coordinate derivation after a certified coordinate change. Inverse transport converts that derivation into a verified solution of the original instance. Increasing next-token entropy is not guaranteed to reach this basin because doing so may require a long sequence of individually low-probability choices; changing the task representation can enter it directly while leaving the policy nearly deterministic.

The scheduling signal is most likely to degenerate when all representations reach the same canonical states, or when normalization collapses states too aggressively. In the first case, every divergence score becomes zero and the specified uniform fallback recovers ordinary search over exact symmetries; learning remains correct, although no efficiency gain is claimed. In the second case, the method may miss useful diversity but cannot invent it, because only verifier-derived states are compared and correctness still requires final inverse verification. Conversely, excessively fine fingerprints could mistake irrelevant state differences for novelty. Restricting fingerprints to normalized open obligations and verifier-certified facts relevant to them removes notation and commentary, while the uniform budget floor limits the cost of residual false novelty.

The claim is therefore deliberately conditional and testable: when certified equivalent presentations cause a model to visit different semantic reasoning states, dynamic coverage scheduling should discover more verified solution paths per rollout token than uniform transformed search or entropy-based sampling. When they do not, the procedure reduces to safe uniform search and produces no false training signal.

final_idea_core.core_claim: Instead of increasing token entropy or perturbing parameters, the system dynamically schedules compute based on the marginal coverage and separation of canonical intermediate reasoning states across multiple certified equivalent problem representations.
final_idea_core.mechanism: Search is conducted over certified symmetries of the problem itself, where equivalent problem transformations are used to elicit different reasoning paths from the same low-entropy model, and intermediate states are mapped to a common canonical space for…
final_idea_core.problem_targeted: Deterministic policies often plateau because they search within a single policy induced by one problem representation, making it difficult to escape local optima that require long, low-probability token sequences.
final_idea_core.source_gap: Certified equivalent problem presentations can cause a language model to visit genuinely different semantic reasoning states and solution basins that are otherwise unreachable by incremental policy changes.
final_idea_core.expected_effect: Dynamic coverage scheduling across certified problem symmetries will discover more verified solution paths per rollout token compared to uniform transformed search or entropy-based sampling, without introducing false positive training signals.

idea_text:
Outcome-based reinforcement learning wastes successful reasoning fragments: a rollout that fails at its final step receives little useful credit even when its prefix reaches a valuable intermediate state, while another rollout may contain a successful continuation from the same state. The obvious approach is to learn a process-reward model that predicts which steps are promising. That introduces an unverifiable learned signal and can reinforce plausible-looking mistakes. Instead, the proposed research would make credit transfer a symbolic operation whose validity is checked by construction.

The setting is reasoning that can be executed by a proof assistant, program interpreter, or other deterministic state machine. Every generated step is replayed to obtain a canonical machine state: the remaining goals, local assumptions, variable scopes, and relevant environment. Across all rollouts and training problems, the system stores transitions between these states, including transitions from rollouts whose overall answer was wrong. Two states are considered interchangeable only when the underlying checker establishes their equivalence after hygienic variable renaming and normalization; embedding similarity is never sufficient.

Training examples are assembled by splicing a prefix ending at state \(s\) to a continuation previously shown to solve an equivalent state \(s'\). Names and local references in the continuation are transported through the checker-provided correspondence, and the entire assembled trajectory is replayed from the original problem. It enters training only if every transition and the final answer verify. Thus a failed rollout can contribute a useful prefix, and a continuation discovered elsewhere can supply its missing credit. The model is trained on verified splices alongside newly sampled trajectories. To avoid merely duplicating common proofs, sampling prioritizes edges that convert previously dead-end prefixes into completed trajectories and state equivalence classes reached by many failures but few successes.

The central causal lever is not greater token entropy, parameter perturbation, or alternative presentations of a problem. It changes the unit over which experience is reused: reward is transferred between trajectories at checker-equivalent intermediate states. If a prefix and suffix meet at the same formal state, their composition is a valid candidate regardless of why either was generated; full replay then removes failures caused by hidden state, scope, or normalization differences. This is analogous to joining paths in an explicitly observed state graph rather than estimating latent step quality.

The most likely degeneracy is that independently generated trajectories rarely encounter exactly matching intermediate states. The study should therefore distinguish literal matches from checker-certified equivalence and measure the internal-state match rate before claiming gains. Canonicalization can merge syntactic variants and common lemma boundaries, but it must not relax equivalence to semantic similarity. If internal matches remain sparse, the mechanism safely reduces to ordinary verified training rather than creating false supervision; its expected advantage is specifically predicted for corpora with recurring formal subgoals. Evaluation would compare verified solutions obtained per newly executed rollout against outcome-only RL, process-reward training, and retrieval of whole demonstrations, while separately reporting how much improvement comes from rescued failed prefixes, cross-problem splices, and exact duplicate paths.

final_idea_core.core_claim: Instead of learning an implicit process-reward model, this approach uses symbolic, checker-validated state equivalence to enable explicit, verified splicing of successful continuations onto dead-end prefixes.
final_idea_core.mechanism: Credit is transferred between reasoning trajectories by splicing a failed prefix with a successful suffix at formally equivalent intermediate states, verified through replay by a deterministic checker.
final_idea_core.problem_targeted: Reinforcement learning for proof-assistant-like reasoning wastes successful reasoning fragments within otherwise failed rollouts, leading to inefficient credit assignment.
final_idea_core.source_gap: Reasoning tasks in deterministic state machines frequently exhibit checker-equivalent intermediate states across different rollouts or problems, making symbolic splicing a viable strategy.
final_idea_core.expected_effect: The system will achieve higher rates of verified solutions per newly executed rollout compared to outcome-only RL, process-reward training, and whole demonstration retrieval, particularly for problems with recurring formal subgoals.

idea_text:
Quantization methods minimize weight or activation error, but reasoning systems are judged by discrete search outcomes. A tiny logit perturbation can redirect an early proof branch and destroy a correct solution, while a large tensor error may be harmless if it changes no search decision. The proposed research therefore treats a bounded reasoning workload as a program-compilation target: compress the model while preserving its complete discrete execution trace, rather than approximating its tensors.

First declare a finite prompt suite, deterministic decoding or tree search, a token horizon, deterministic tool and verifier behavior, and bitwise-deterministic inference kernels. Run the full-precision model and record every expanded prefix, token ranking used by the search, branch order, stopping decision, tool call, verifier interaction, and final output. Each discrete decision becomes a set of logit inequalities. For greedy decoding, if token \(y\) was selected at prefix \(x\), require
\[
z_y(x;q)\ge z_j(x;q)+\epsilon_{xj}
\]
for every competing token \(j\), where \(q\) is the block-precision assignment. For beam or top-\(k\) search, impose the corresponding membership and ordering inequalities at every selection boundary. Ties are governed by the declared implementation’s deterministic tie-breaking rule; margins may be zero when exact ordering preservation, rather than robustness, is the goal.

The model is partitioned into fixed weight blocks, and each block has a finite menu of representations, such as 2-, 3-, 4-, 8-, 16-bit, and original precision. The compiler seeks the minimum-memory precision assignment whose actual deterministic execution satisfies all currently collected decision inequalities. Crucially, it does not use gradient attribution to guess which blocks caused a divergence. Gradients are the obvious competent approach, but they can be zero, locally misleading near quantization thresholds, or unable to represent interactions among blocks. Instead, attribution is defined by an exact finite constraint search over precision assignments.

Concretely, when execution first diverges at a shared prefix \(x\), the system adds all inequalities encoding the reference decision at \(x\) to a constraint set \(C\). It then solves
\[
q^\star=\arg\min_{q\in\mathcal Q^B} \operatorname{Memory}(q)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
g_c(q)\ge 0\;\;\forall c\in C,
\]
where \(B\) is the number of blocks, \(\mathcal Q\) is the finite precision menu, and every \(g_c(q)\) is evaluated by actually running the model at the relevant recorded prefix. Thus, the blocks “blamed” for a divergence are precisely those assigned higher precision in the minimum-memory feasible assignment, relative to the previous assignment. This is a behavioral witness set, not a sensitivity estimate.

An exact branch-and-bound implementation enumerates precision assignments in increasing memory order. For each complete assignment, it evaluates all accumulated prefixes and rejects the assignment at its first violated inequality. The first feasible assignment is therefore memory-optimal within the declared block partition and precision menu; lexicographic block order gives deterministic tie-breaking. Partial assignments may be pruned only using sound interval bounds on the remaining logits. If such bounds are unavailable or loose, no pruning is performed—exhaustive enumeration remains the defining algorithm. Feasibility is non-gating because the research question concerns whether exact behavioral compilation exposes compression unavailable to numerical-error objectives.

This inner optimization automatically handles non-additive interactions. A divergence might be repaired only when two blocks are promoted together, or promoting one block might undo the benefit of promoting another. Single-block gradients or greedy restoration would miss these cases, whereas complete constraint search tests joint assignments directly. It also prevents repairs for later counterexamples from silently invalidating earlier ones, because every recompilation must satisfy the entire accumulated constraint set, not merely the newest margin.

Constraints from the reference trace alone are insufficient because a compressed model can enter a prefix never visited by the reference. The outer loop therefore uses counterexample-guided compilation:

1. Solve the finite minimum-memory problem for all inequalities currently in \(C\).
2. Run the complete bounded search procedure with that compressed model.
3. Compare its execution against the full-precision reference and locate the earliest differing discrete decision.
4. Add the reference inequalities at that shared prefix to \(C\), then solve the global precision-assignment problem again.
5. Stop only when the complete bounded executions are identical.

The loop terminates by construction. There are finitely many precision assignments and finitely many bounded execution decisions. More importantly, the all-full-precision assignment always satisfies every reference inequality under the declared deterministic runtime. Each counterexample excludes the current assignment, and the solver never needs to discard previously added constraints. Consequently, either a compressed feasible assignment is found or the procedure converges to full precision.

The attribution step most likely to degenerate is local sensitivity: all blocks may have zero or misleading first-order influence even though a joint precision change repairs the decision. The proposed algorithm contains no such signal. Its oracle is the violated decision inequality under an actual candidate representation, and exhaustive joint search remains informative whenever any feasible assignment exists. The only possible degeneracy is substantive rather than algorithmic: the minimum feasible assignment may retain nearly every block at high precision. That yields a low compression ratio and demonstrates that the declared workload is not safely compressible under the chosen formats; it does not weaken the trace-equivalence guarantee.

The resulting guarantee is intentionally workload-specific. For the declared prompts, bounded search procedure, precision menu, and deterministic runtime, the compressed model explores exactly the same branches, makes the same tool and verifier calls, and returns the same answers as the full-precision model. No claim is made for unseen prompts, although held-out traces can measure empirical transfer.

Experiments should compare this compilation objective against weight-error quantization, activation-aware quantization, and ordinary mixed precision at matched memory. Primary measurements are achieved compression, exact trace-equivalence rate, earliest-divergence depth, and catastrophic final-answer changes. The central conceptual leap remains distinct from ordinary attribution-based quantization: rather than estimating which tensors numerically matter, the method searches for the least-memory machine representation that preserves the bounded discrete execution semantics of the neural reasoner.
